column1: # Per-assembly line-coverage floors, BY PROFILE.
# WHY TWO PROFILES AND NOT ONE
# CI and a developer machine run genuinely different test populations, so one
# number cannot serve both. Measured 2026-08-09 on Excise.Rendering:
#     ci    (corpus-less runner)          78.4%
#     full  (corpora + mutool/gs/cairo)   87.0%
# The 8.6-point gap is entirely Differential and Corpus tests, which cannot run
# without the gitignored corpora and the reference renderers. A single floor is
# wrong in both directions:
#   * set at 87% -> CI fails on every run, forever
#   * set at 78% -> a regression that only shows in the differential tests
#                   passes silently, and those are the tests that exist because
#                   excise must not be its own oracle
# This mirrors the skip-allowlist's environment conditioning (#854), which
# exists for the same reason: the allowlist is calibrated for a corpus-LESS
# runner, and entries declare what they need in order to run.
# HOW FLOORS ARE CHOSEN
# ~2 points below the measured value. Tight enough to catch a real regression,
# loose enough not to flap on ordinary variation (a test moved between filters,
# a branch counted differently). Floors RATCHET UP as coverage improves; they do
# not drift down. Raising one is a normal part of improving coverage. Lowering
# one requires saying why in the commit message.
# THE FAILURE MODE TO WATCH
# The `ci` floor is the one enforced on every push, so it is the one that gets
# attention. `full` is enforced by the release path (t2/release-smoke), which
# runs far less often — so `full` is where rot hides. If `full` and `ci` ever
# converge, that is not coverage improving; it is the differential tests having
# stopped contributing, and it should be investigated rather than celebrated.
# Format:  profile <TAB> assembly <TAB> floor <TAB> measured <TAB> note
# Regenerate measurements with scripts/measure-coverage.sh
